properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued September 13 at 3:07PM EDT by NWS Binghamton NY
properties.description:
At 307 PM EDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
Weedsport, or 8 miles north of Auburn, moving east at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and half inch hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Van Buren, Baldwinsville, Sennett, Skaneateles, Marcellus, Jordan,
Amboy, Camillus, Elbridge, and Bennetts Corners.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

This storm may intensify, so be certain to monitor local radio
stations and available television stations for additional information
and possible warnings from the National Weather Service.

properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued September 13 at 3:03PM EDT until September 13 at 3:30PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Biscayne Bay...
Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM...

* Until 330 PM EDT.

* At 303 PM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located near Soldier Key,
moving east at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Soldier Key, Key Biscayne, Cape Florida, and Coral Gables.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.
properties.area: Biscayne Bay; Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued September 13 at 2:58PM EDT until September 13 at 5:00PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...West Central Highlands County in south central Florida...

* WHEN...Until 500 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 258 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Between 2.5 and 3.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Lake Placid, Sylvan Shores, Lake Josephine and Placid Lakes.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued September 13 at 12:58PM MDT until September 13 at 4:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern San Miguel County in northeastern New
Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 400 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos. Dangerous flows
over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1258 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to slow
moving thunderstorms near Cowles. This will cause arroyo and
small stream flooding. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.5 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Cowles and Tererro.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
In hilly or mountainous terrain there are numerous low water
crossings which are potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued September 13 at 11:35AM MST until September 13 at 1:30PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
At 1135 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated that heavy rain has moved
east of the Havasupai Creek drainage north of Supai, though
additional storms are possible through the afternoon. Between 0.5 and
1 inch of rain fell earlier this morning. Flash flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Beaver Falls, Mooney Falls and Little Navajo Falls.

This includes the Colorado River between river miles 156 and 158.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Second Chance Camp Site.

This includes the following swimming holes...
All swimming holes on Havasu Creek near Supai.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Sinyella Canyon, Colorado River, Little Coyote Canyon and Havasu
Creek.
properties.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, including Havasupai Creek.

Get out of washes and creeks if you are camping or hiking! Flooding
is occurring or imminent and will inundate creeks and washes.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued September 13 at 2:32PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Biscayne Bay...
Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM...

At 232 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a strong thunderstorm, capable
of producing winds to around 30 knots. This thunderstorm was located
near Biscayne Bay, moving east at 15 knots.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots and locally higher
waves. Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until this storm
passes.
properties.area: Biscayne Bay; Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued September 13 at 2:26PM EDT until September 13 at 5:30PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Miami-Dade County in southeastern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 530 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 225 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Homestead, Homestead Miami Speedway, Homestead Base, Princeton,
Goulds, Cutler Bay, West Perrine, Palmetto Bay, Richmond Heights,
South Miami Heights, Palmetto Estates and Howard.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued September 13 at 11:14AM MST until September 13 at 2:15PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 215 PM MST.

* At 1114 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area, on the far east side of Chino
Valley including the Granite Creek drainage. Between 1 and 1.75
inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1
inch are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
East side of Chino Valley.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Granite Creek, Little Chino Valley and Verde River.
properties.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern Lee County in southwestern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 345 PM EDT.

Water over roadways.

Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen.

Suncoast Estates and North Fort Myers.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued September 13 at 9:57AM EDT until September 13 at 4:00PM EDT by NWS Upton NY
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Upton has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in New Jersey...

Saddle River near Lodi affecting Bergen County.

For the Saddle River...including Lodi...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Saddle River near Lodi.

* WHEN...From this morning to this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 5.5 feet, Saddle River begins to overflow into the
back parking lot of the Boys and Girls club.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 AM EDT Sunday the stage was 5.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
afternoon to a crest of 5.7 feet this afternoon. It will then
fall below flood stage this afternoon.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.1
feet on 01/27/1996.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 400 PM EDT.
